claims.statement: The currently listed addressable Polish private online-betting market consists of 17 licensed operators, alongside state-monopoly online casino and number games.
Polish law mandates operator-level responsible-gambling policies and controls but the reviewed provisions do not provide the proposed shared status rail.
A major Polish operator currently offers an account-specific three-month self-exclusion.
EU policy has explicitly encouraged national self-exclusion registers and operator consultation of them.
Britain and Sweden operate cross-operator checks at registration or login, proving technical feasibility at national scale.
Those comparators derive coverage from licence or statutory obligations, so they do not validate voluntary network formation in Poland.
A consent-only design faces unresolved validity, withdrawal, profiling, and automated-decision questions under GDPR guidance.
A regulator- or association-sponsored utility with a minimal yes/no response is the more credible structure than a voluntary shared risk score.
No reviewed evidence establishes Polish regulator sponsorship, operator commitments, procurement price, or a lawful controller model.

contrary_evidence: c704-s1 provides no reviewed national shared-registry mandate.
c704-s3 shows an operator can satisfy a baseline self-exclusion workflow internally.
c704-s7 through c704-s9 show that successful network coverage is compulsory, not merely attractive to operators.
c704-s5 and c704-s6 make a simplistic consent token legally insufficient without a full purpose, basis, rights, and governance analysis.
